context: overnight lead generation, email campaign prep
goal: Determine the most effective cold-email structure/tactic before drafting any outreach
method: Dedicated research agent tasked with finding real sourced data (not generic advice) on cold-email psychology, personalization impact on reply rate, CTA softness vs hardness, length, subject lines
key_finding: Soft CTAs beat hard CTAs ~3x in reply rate (4.2% vs 1.4%, Puzzle Inbox, 200k+ emails, same copy/only CTA varied). Personalized emails get 2-3x the reply rate of generic ones across 3 independent datasets (Hunter.io 11M, Woodpecker 20M, Interseller 1M+ emails).
decision_driven: Every drafted email follows: specific observation -> genuine value -> one-sentence bridge -> soft close. Never leads with the offer/pitch.

outcome: rejected_batch
reasoning: Research agent found real demand signal (live Freelancer.com job postings) but the platform deliberately anonymizes client contact details, and Reddit/LinkedIn (where an owner might self-identify) weren't reachable without a logged-in session. Agent explicitly declined to pad the list with guessed emails to hit a target count.
criteria_applied: A lead only counts as usable if the email is verified directly from a source, never inferred from a naming pattern or platform username.

context: live website enquiry-form failure, reported by Owner's test
decision: Root-caused a real live 500 error a test user hit submitting the contact form. Three compounding causes, found in sequence by testing the actual production path (not just locally): (1) my own earlier hub restart lost the WEBSITE_WEBHOOK_SECRET env var that was only ever manually exported, never persisted -- fixed by generating and persisting a new one the same way HUB_PASSWORD already is; (2) HUB_HOST bound Flask to the single Tailscale IP only, not localhost, so Tailscale Funnel's own localhost:5000 proxy target got nothing -- every webhook call 502'd regardless of secret; fixed by binding 0.0.0.0. (3) Render's HUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET env var still needs manual updating to match the newly regenerated secret -- flagged to Owner, cannot do myself.
method: Tested the actual public https://watersandco.info/enquire endpoint directly via curl (not just the local hub) to reproduce the exact 500 the Owner's tester saw, then traced the chain (Funnel proxy target vs actual bind address) with ss/curl at each hop rather than guessing.
root_cause_ownership: The (1) cause was my own error from an earlier ad-hoc restart that didn't preserve production env vars. Owning it plainly rather than only fixing forward.
lesson: When restarting a long-running production process, always use its own documented launcher (launch_hub.sh), never an ad-hoc command in a bare shell -- env vars that were only ever manually exported are invisible and get silently lost.

method: Dispatched two independent, genuinely exhaustive (not sampled) subagent audits -- one per Flask app -- each instructed to read every file in full and show its work per check rather than assert cleanliness. context: Senior Tech Concierge price raise, Owner's request ("put tech concierge up to $99/hr? or find a reasonable equivalent")
decision: Raised in-person to $99/hr (was $79), held remote at $69/hr (was $59, deliberately NOT raised to $99 in step), extended 90min to $145 (was $119), 30min follow-up to $49 (was $45).
method: Re-verified competitor pricing live rather than trusting the 2026-08-06 research pass. Found the key structural point the earlier pass had missed: in-person and remote compete in different markets. In-person is Perth-only (travel radius) -- real alternatives are Geeks2U ($158/hr Home, re-confirmed direct from geeks2u.com.au/pricing) and IT 4 Retirees (~$235/hr effective with travel), so $99 is a 37-58% undercut with headroom. Remote is Australia-wide -- competes against a denser $59-100/hr interstate field (Dtech, Fixable, IT Help at Home, Seniors Tech and Tea, My Senior IT) with no travel cost to justify a bigger jump, so it was held back rather than raised in step. Rejected a call-out/minimum-booking structure (what Geeks2U does) because it would contradict the live site's 'no one-hour minimums' promise and destroy the line's sharpest differentiator.
outcome: Applied to website/webapp/config.py and ops-hub/app/config.py RATE_CARD (72 -> 85, blended), wave3-unscoped/tech_concierge/pricing_sheet.md, and PRICING.md row 13. Independently re-verified again (Geeks2U, Fixable, My Senior IT) before the Owner's follow-up question 'are these prices ok and not too low' -- all three matched. Pushed live, confirmed on watersandco.info.
lesson: Splitting a single service into channel-specific pricing (in-person vs remote) only becomes obvious once you separate which competitors actually compete in each channel -- a blended single rate had been masking that in-person had far more headroom than remote.

lesson: This will keep happening on every .py (and intermittently .html/.gitignore) edit in this repo until someone runs the Semgrep login from a real interactive terminal where a browser can complete the OAuth callback -- flagged to the Owner as a standing to-do, not something an agent session can resolve on its own.

context: Owner asked to triple-check all 117 drafted emails against current pricing, fold in today's research, re-verify anti-spam law, and find new legal client-acquisition channels
decision: Pulled all 117 drafts directly from the connected Gmail account (not the repo's copies) via list_drafts across 3 pages -- verified zero contain a dollar figure in the body, so none could be stale on price and nothing needed re-drafting.
method: Re-verified the Spam Act 2003 live against AustLII's Schedule 2 statutory text and ACMA's published consent-expectations statement rather than relying on the earlier session's summary. Confirmed: inferred consent requires ALL of -- the address reaches a specific role-holder, is conspicuously published, it's reasonable to assume that publication had the person's agreement, AND the message is relevant to that role. Mere publication of an address is explicitly not sufficient on its own. Current outreach practice (small hand-qualified batches against a real business signal, never a scraped list) already matches this -- no compliance gap found.
outcome: Wrote wave3-unscoped/lead_generation/legal_channels_not_yet_tried_2026-08-09.md with 8 new legal channels (own GBP, trade-supplier noticeboards, Chamber of Commerce, hipages/ServiceSeeking listings, organic FB group participation, activating existing-client referral asks, partner content-swaps, local classifieds), each with the specific legal basis for why it's compliant. Flagged the 2026-08-05 SMS ready-list as needing the same consent check before any outbound use -- SMS carries identical Spam Act rules, a common misconception is that it's a lighter-touch channel.
lesson: Verifying a compliance question 'live' rather than trusting a prior session's summary is worth the extra tool calls even when the prior summary turns out correct -- the cost of being wrong on Spam Act compliance (penalties up to ~$313k+) is asymmetric enough to justify re-checking every time it materially matters, not just once.

context: landing page hero headline -- Owner found 'enquiries' confusing in the original copy
decision: Iterated through several rounds with the Owner before landing on: H1 'Find and fix what's quietly costing your business time, jobs and opportunities.' / lead paragraph 'Waters & Co identifies where enquiries are missed, follow-up slows and administration gets stuck -- then implements practical systems and AI-assisted workflows with clear human oversight.'
method: Original: 'Fix the workflow that is costing your business time or enquiries.' Owner flagged 'enquiries' as confusing. First attempt over-corrected into a full 3-item symptom list in the H1 itself; Owner narrowed scope back to a single-word swap ('missed calls'). Owner then separately proposed working toward implying financial upside without literally saying 'money' -- flagged 'money' as a claim that reads as a promised financial/business outcome (same category the existing 'no guaranteed financial or business result' rule and ACL misleading-conduct risk already cover), recommended loss-framing ('jobs and opportunities') over gain-framing as the compliant way to get the same psychological effect. Owner then supplied their own final draft, which relocated the concrete explanation from the H1 into the lead paragraph instead -- a genuinely better structural choice (short punchy H1, explanatory subhead) that this session's own drafts hadn't tried.
outcome: Applied, verified live on watersandco.info after push.
lesson: Flask's dev server (debug=False) does not auto-reload Jinja templates -- caused two rounds of showing the Owner stale text via the browser preview mid-workshop until traced to app.jinja_env.auto_reload defaulting to app.debug. Worth restarting the local server after every template edit during any future copy-workshop session, not just after code changes.
correction: The 'money' vs loss-framing distinction is a reusable pattern for this business specifically -- any future headline/copy work should default to naming the concrete thing being lost (a job, a call, a review) rather than the implied financial gain, without being asked each time.
